claims.text: The targeted material family is fcc high-entropy alloys based on Fe-Co-Ni, including CoCrFeMnNi and Co40Fe25Cr20Ni15.
The targeted property is enhanced strength-ductility synergy, particularly under cryogenic conditions.
Controlling stacking-fault energy enhances cryogenic strength-ductility synergy.
Magnetic and orbital moments in multicomponent fcc alloys are highly sensitive to local chemical ordering and short-range order.
Cr moments align antiferromagnetically relative to their local coordination shell and reduce the net magnetic moment.
The orbital-moment contribution to total magnetization and its coupling to lattice distortion remain poorly quantified.
CrMnFeCoNi exhibits paramagnetic-to-spin-glass and spin-glass-to-ferromagnetic transitions at approximately 93 K and 38 K, respectively.
Changing Fe, Co, Ni, and Cr concentrations can tune stacking-fault energy, with Co and Cr decreasing it and Fe and Ni increasing it.
Cold rolling and annealing can induce selected short-range chemical order and thereby improve mechanical properties while managing magnetic state.
Stacking-fault energy mediates the competition between dislocation slip and mechanical twinning.
Short-range chemical order influences magnetic exchange interactions in these alloys.
Atomic-size mismatch produces lattice distortion in fcc high-entropy alloys.
Variations in Fe, Co, and Ni local coordination alter crystal-field splitting and orbital-angular-momentum quenching.
The orbital moment fluctuates with local coordination rather than being a fixed material constant.
Orbital-moment fluctuations affect the electronic contribution to stacking-fault energy and thereby the slip-versus-twinning transition.
Although smaller than the spin moment, the orbital moment can contribute significantly to magnetic anisotropy and magnetoelastic coupling.
A tailored fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based alloy will achieve elongation above 50% and yield strength above 400 MPa at cryogenic temperatures.
Standard equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has approximately 410 MPa strength and 50% elongation at room temperature.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms a chemically disordered fcc solid solution at ambient pressure.
The orbital contribution to magnetization will be nonlinear and strongly dependent on short-range chemical order.
